This procedure outlines the major 
maintenance procedure P2, which must be performed from eight to twelve years, 
Y8:12 as indicated in the above titled block.

The first draft initiated 
at Demo substation, eng Abdel Tawab Ramadan. The first review at Nov 2007.

items: A work permit must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category,

Safety fence
 with cautions marks surrounding the work area is required.
Ensure that the CB isolated and proper earthing at the two sides of CB is required.

Interrupt
 remote control and motor circuits (this achieved by receiving the multi-pin
 plug at the left hand side at the operating mechanism)

Switch breaker
 ON and OFF manually in order to discharge the closing and springs.

Safety equipment "belt,
 shoes,...,etc".

Drain the 
 SF6
 gas from CB until 0.15 bar

Opening of CB as following:
 - Before opening CB insure that the CB is in the open
 position and that the closing spring is discharged.
 - Disconnect the operating linkage between CB and
 operating mechanism, leave it adjusted.
 - Withdraw the break with the aid of the maintenance trolley
 see fig (4)

Coars cleaning: Vacuum clean the break; the inside of the CB enclosure and insulated
 components immediately.

Important:
 - Person who perform this task must wear throw away
 overall ; gloves and gas mask
 - Avoid skin-contact with decomposition products.

Cleaning of individual components as following:
 - Insulators: core insulators (8), supporting rods
 (20), pull rods (16) and tie rods (22) figure 1. These items are always 
 to be cleaned first with vacuum cleaned
 and with isopropyl or ethylalchol.
 - Metallic component:- clean all items as soon as
 possible after opening the CB to reduce the affects of reaction 
 products the cleaning by vacuum cleaner
 and isopropyl or ethylalchol

Adsorbed:
 Remove the adsorbed after opening the CB a new adsorbed must be replaced
 shortly before reclosing the CB.

Contact
 reconditioning : as following (see figures 2, 3) 
 - Dismantling arcing rod (46) as follow
 - Remove cylindrical head screw (92) of blast - cylinder
 (52).
 - Shift blast - cylinder (52) toward rear.
 - Remove complete nozzle base (42)
 - Dismantle arcing rod (46).

Dismantling
 arcing sleeve (39) as following. figures 1, 2
 - Remove tie rod (22) 
 - Dismantle cylinder support (43)
 - Remove current carrying cylinder (38) loosen bolt (33)
 - Loosen nut (41). Remove arcing sleeve (39)

Loose items
 - Push out blast nozzle (51) from cylinder support (43)
 - Flow guides (45)
 - O ring (53)

Assessment of
 arcing rod (46):
 - Replace when permissible limit is exceeded
 fig (5) or when pitting at tip or deep scores are visible (
 frictional 
 traces are permissible )

Assessment of
 arcing sleeve (39)
 - Replace when permissible limits is
 exceeded and when pitting at tip is visible see fig (8)
 - Blast - nozzle (51):
 - Replace when specified limit is exceeded or break down traces are
 visible along or across the nozzle see fig (7) 
 - Assessment of flow guide (54)
 - Replace when specified limit is exceeded or
 break downs along or across the guide.
 - Assessment of absorber (87); O-ring (53) always to be replaced.

Assembly as
 following
 - Fit arcing sleeve (39) in current carrying cylinder (38) 
 tightening torque 80 Nm for nut (41)
 - Fit flow guide (45) and arcing rod (46) to nozzle base plate
 (42); tightening torque for bolt (48) 40 Nm
 - The clamping plate (47) must not rotate when tightening the
 arcing rod (46). The spring pin (49) must fit into the 
 hold of clamping plate.
 - The flow guide (45) must have no play.

Fit O ring
 (53); blast nozzle (51), complete nozzle base (420 and blast cylinder (52)
 to cylinder support (50)

Insert
 complete current carrying cylinder into guide cylinder (29) and screw
 together with cross bar (37) at front. Don't tighten hex head bolts (33).
 Lubricate contact sliding surfaces.

Refit cylinder
 support (50) and tie rods (22)

Operate
 switching lever in close direction until arcing contacts (46) and (39)
 engage and current carrying cylinder (38) rests approx. 5-10 mm before the
 shielding cap. Tighten hex head bolts (33) fig (19)

Measure
 contact resistance
 - Measurement: position as for (6-2-f) (current carrying
 cylinder not engaged )
 - Measurement: fully closed permissible value max
 55 ohm
 - Different between 1 to 2 measurement <
 30 ohm if contact resistance are too high.
 - Measure individual contact points and
 clean them thoroughly.
 - Assemble absorber (87); gasket-ring (81) and close the
 circuit breaker

Check up
 stroke as mentioned before (operational check up after 5 years).

Make vacuum
 for CB until approx. 4 mbar (about 6 hours)
Check leakage.

Fill
 SF6 gas
 up to rated pressure.

Enter the
 recorded values in the inspection record.

Repeat the
 steps (1) to (11) for the remaining two poles.

Measure
 operating time for CB and compare with commissioning value and record the
 values in the inspection record.

rows:
Gas
 compartment switchgear at
 rated voltage

items:
ppmv = water content in "parts per million" referred
 to volume (values referred to mass or weight in ppmg van be
 converted with a factor of 8.1) 
 "Dew point chart see figure 8"

The dew point is valid for the 
 operating pressure range between filling pressure and minimum rating pressure.
 see figure 11
